reviewer: Codex parent session; independent of the fixture-generation invocation

findings.bullet: - app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file leaves `app.startup.load_defaults()` reading a nonexistent `defaults.json` on every invocation — Loading bundled defaults raises `FileNotFoundError` instead of returning the default timeout.
findings.reason: Names the deleted defaults file, its unchanged load_defaults consumer, and FileNotFoundError on invocation; the base-side citation matches the deletion.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns false because the upper bound uses `< 65535` — Callers reject port 65535 despite the documented inclusive range.
findings.reason: Identifies input 65535 and the exclusive upper bound, explaining rejection of a valid TCP port.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `load_config` catches every `Exception`, including missing-file, permission, and malformed-JSON errors, and returns `{}` without a diagnostic or an adjacent explanation of the fallback — Callers cannot distinguish failed configuration loading from a successfully loaded empty configuration.
findings.reason: Names realistic file/JSON errors that become an indistinguishable empty configuration, with no caller diagnostic.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:38 — tests — No existing or added test exercises trailing-dot removal, such as `normalize_host("Example.COM.")`; the added test only checks lowercasing — A regression leaving the trailing dot intact would pass the current tests.
findings.reason: Identifies the untested trailing-dot branch and a concrete stripping regression that the existing lowercase-only test misses; credit is for that distinct branch.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” but the empty-input branch executes `return ""` — Callers following the documentation and checking for `None` will fail to recognize an empty host.
findings.reason: Contrasts the promised None with the actual empty-string result and explains how callers checking for None are misled.
